video_title: Ray Allen Breaks Down What's WRONG With Modern Basketball

quotes.speaker: Brice Butler
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Allen on the lost art of basketball in the modern era
quotes.excerpt: a lot of guys have lost the art of what basketball should actually look like

text_blocks.speaker: Brice Butler
text_blocks.text: When you look at today's game, obviously when you played, I feel like there was a level of art in the game of basketball and now, my opinion is that a lot of guys just settle to shoot threes. So when you look at the game, do you look at it for the evolution and say, oh, that's just where we're at right now, or you're like, no, a lot of guys have lost the art of what basketball should actually look like?

text_blocks.speaker: Ray Allen
text_blocks.text: When you're young and you're coming to the game, everybody's running the motion offense and you're setting screens and back-door cuts and you're making four and five passes and you get to see, it becomes a machine. You see how a team works and it's so, you know, Princeton used to run that motion offense and they always got a back-door layup with Pete Carroll and it was just like, man, they were so good because they cut hard, they set screens and you couldn't take shortcuts. And that's basketball. It's not about the one great player, it's about the sum of all five.

quotes.speaker: Ray Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Allen on the decline of mid-range and post-up play
quotes.excerpt: we've lost the mid-range game and I hear coaches yelling no mid-range shots
quotes.quote: What's happened is we've lost the mid-range game and I hear coaches yelling no mid-range shots. And then we've lost post-up players. Bigs don't even have a place in the game anymore. That to me is the tragedy because now what we do is we have these guys that work in basketball offices that are analytic guys that sit here and say why we need to shoot more threes than twos. And they just they convince the upper management and everybody else that guys that never played the game, you should be shooting more threes than twos. And I just think, and here's the thing, here's the proof. Okay, so Golden State won, they shoot a lot of threes and Boston won and they shot a lot of threes and they lost because they shot a lot of threes as well. But this past year, look at Oklahoma City and Indiana. Both had guys that could shoot threes because you need three-point shooters out there and you set the game up, but they were killing on pick and roll in the mid-range. Yes. So when I came in the game, you had some incredible pick and roll players. You had some incredible mid-range guys. It was it was insane. You could learn so much from these these dudes and the game is just we've lost that. And that's an art.

quotes.speaker: Ray Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Allen laments the lack of big men in modern basketball
quotes.excerpt: I'm devastated about all the big men that don't have a place in the game anymore
quotes.quote: One of the things that I'm devastated about is all the big men that don't have a place in the game anymore. It used to be amazing to watch guys score. We used to throw the ball in the block and guys could score or you got to be a great passer out of the post. Two-man game. Like, it's arguable who the best power forward of all time is. A lot of people will say Tim Duncan. We'll never see another Tim Duncan again the way the game is played right now because we've taken that from the big players, the big guys, because we won't allow, coaches aren't playing this throw the ball in and out. I like shooting threes and that was something I I like driving to the hole. I love pick and roll. I love posting up. So I would assume or I would think that it will revert back at some point because there's going to be some bigs that come along where you got to just because they're too good.

quotes.speaker: Ray Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Ray Allen on the lack of patience for player development
quotes.excerpt: you're never almost allowed to develop your guys, you got to win now
quotes.quote: I just don't think the development of players is you see a lot of coaches because now we're in an era where coaches have to win right away. Because you have to remember, if you look at in the last couple of years, like Mike Budenholzer got fired, he brought Milwaukee a championship, they hadn't won since the 70s and he got fired. Monty Williams went to Phoenix, brought them to the finals, he gets fired. Then gets the largest contract in the history of the league by Detroit and they fire him there. So there's so many examples of coaches getting fired and then getting rehired in other places. So you're never almost allowed to develop your guys, you got to win now. Because if you have, if there's a semblance of, you know, like a lull somewhere in your organization, you get fired because there's an impatience in organizations. You just got to bring the guys in, you make a lot of money, we got to we got to start winning now. And so the turnover in coaches and you see it in college too, they're not they're not having patience to watch develop and so in college, coaches aren't taking projects anymore. Not developing these kids, I'm going to get somebody who's been two, three years in college already. So I don't have to do much. You go out there and run pick and rolls and get us some buckets.
